Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestSymmetry010Chronology_badLeapDayDates.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestSymmetry010Chronology/TestSymmetry010Chronology_badLeapDayDates.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The original test is dominated by ~80 lines of unused data-provider methods (and many unused imports); only `data_badLeapDates` and the single `badLeapDayDates` test actually run. I'll produce a focused, well-documented version that preserves the exact runtime behavior.Compilation succeeded (`COMPILE_OK`). I refactored the test to keep only the live code path — the single parameterized `badLeapDayDates` test — removing ~80 lines of unused data providers and unused imports, while giving the data source, method, parameters, and constants descriptive names plus a doc comment explaining the leap-week-day rule. The same call (`Symmetry010Date.of(year, 12, 37)`) with the same years (1, 100, 200, 2000) still asserts a `DateTimeException`, so runtime behavior is unchanged.
